f30734a8cadd8c2e8d823603cca91aa7cb2fc59b: A resort on a human scale, Peisey-Vallandry focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 60 km of runs are ideal for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially with family or for skiers who don't need to constantly renew their playground. Peisey-Vallandry's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It's one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. On snow, Peisey-Vallandry is in a strong position with its highest point at 3,226 m — even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold up well into April. The village at 1,600 m is also well placed to guarantee comfortable conditions from mid-December. The budget for a stay in Peisey-Vallandry is clearly high: 70€ for a day lift pass, on top of which come accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before setting off. In short: Peisey-Vallandry is one of those rare resorts that combines a real village, a sincerely family atmosphere and runs suited to everyone. It's hard to miss your stay here.

f3f7534be703fa16af43d34022a27176d80fd794: Corno alle Scale is a small, understated resort — 14 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Corno alle Scale's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Apennines for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Corno alle Scale's modest altitude — base at 1418 m, summit at 1945 m — makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before you leave is strongly advised. At €38, the day lift pass places Corno alle Scale in the mid-range category on budget — neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short, Corno alle Scale doesn't compete with the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
